hits.name: levelsio
hits.hook: 'Yesterday I spent all day typing this into Claude Code' + the exact prompt + his setup + a new ritual ('security week'). 1,589 bookmarks: people saved it as a checklist.
hits.draft_en:
levelsio wants a "security week" every month. After nearly 30 years in disaster recovery, I'd add a restore day to it.

An audit shows you what's exposed. A restore test shows whether you can come back when something gets through anyway.

The prompt I'd type into Claude Code next:

"Find every backup this server depends on. Walk me through restoring it to a clean box and tell me what breaks."

A backup you've never restored is a guess.
hits.video_tip: 30-45s screen recording: type the restore prompt into Claude Code on a throwaway test VPS, let it run, and cut on the first thing that breaks. Face cam in the corner, no client systems on screen.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.hook: 'Speaking of the devil, now it's Tailscale's turn' + a link to check your setup. Same series format, with an action. 558 bookmarks.
hits.draft_en:
Black October so far: PHP2Shell, the Brotli bug in Node, now Tailscale SSH. Every few days it's someone else's turn.

Patching is half the job. The other half is the 3am question: if this box is gone tomorrow, how long until you're back up?

Four things I'd check before Friday:

1. Is there a copy of your data outside the account that could get popped?
2. When did you last restore it, start to finish?
3. Could you rotate every API key and env var from one list?
4. Who gets the call, and do they know it's them?

Nearly 30 years in DR and the lesson hasn't changed. The outage hurts. A slow, messy recovery hurts more.
hits.video_tip: 40-60s talking head at your desk: put each of the four questions on screen as you say it, then end on 'which one would you fail?' to pull replies.

narrative_synthesis: Black October is the meta: AI-found flaws (PHP2Shell, Brotli in Node, Tailscale SSH) land every few days and builders are turning them into a running series and a monthly 'security week'. Around it: Claude Code workflow posts with the exact prompt, model-race takes (Opus 5.5, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GPT-6), and resilience stories like the Pentagon's 90-day bases. Disaster recovery is the gap nobody in the watchlist is filling: lots of 'patch and audit', almost no 'can you restore'.
